name: Road Trip West
tagline: One Toyota car carries you from Kawasaki via Daikoku, Enoshima, the Hakone Turnpike and Fuji to Osaka and the Suzuka track, and a second car takes you to the Rusutsu drift course, three ski areas, Otaru and Asahiyama.
summary: Three Tokyo nights with a full anime day and the Girls Band Cry walk, then a Toyota car from Kawasaki (Jan 21) to Namba (Jan 24): Daikoku, Enoshima and the Slam Dunk crossing, the Turnpike, Eva's Lake Ashi, Gotemba and a Fuji-view villa. The long Fuji → Osaka day has no Suzuka any more: you drive to the Namba base, see the Nara hill fire by train, and drive to Suzuka on Sunday before you return the car. One Kansai base (4 nights) covers Kyoto, Kobe and Osaka. In Hokkaido (5 nights) a second car links the Rusutsu drift course, Rusutsu, Annupuri and Hirafu skiing (Pegasis teaches Aoki), Otaru, Sapporo and Asahiyama. You fly back to Tokyo on Feb 1 because it is cheaper for both return flights.

who.pegasis: In: Daikoku (he drives, Thu), Hakone Turnpike, Taikanzan, Otome Pass, Gotemba outlets (also his winter-gear stop), Suzuka EV kart, Rusutsu snow drift (he drives), 3 ski days (Rusutsu, Annupuri, Hirafu; he teaches Aoki), Asahiyama penguins, Daruma, Garaku, Moiwa, Nakano, Radio Kaikan, SHELTER live show, Maidreamin, Ikebukuro goods, Nara fire, Isetan half-price, City Hall view, Shinjuku yakitori, Narita bus, and the car road west (Tokaido anime-and-car idea). Out: Onuma (Hakodate side, about 4 h each way from Niseko); the Toyota museums in Nagoya (not on the route). He joins Enoshima (short, morning), Yokohama Chinatown dinner and Otaru as the fair trade for the Turnpike and the drift day, and sleeps in while Aoki does Fushimi Inari.
who.aoki: In: Suga stairs, Akihabara, ZEST, maid cafés (Tokyo, Osaka, Sapporo), Nakano, Shimokitazawa and SHELTER, Girls Band Cry Kawasaki + Yako + Hachiko, Yokohama Chinatown and Cup Noodles, Daikoku with Tatsumi and Umihotaru, Enoshima and the Slam Dunk crossing, Evangelion's Lake Ashi, Lake Kawaguchi, the Hanz Fuji-view villa, Yuru Camp Motosu, Suzuka, Nara, Fushimi Inari at dawn, Kinkakuji, Sabbat (Kyoto, Kobe, Osaka), Namba food, Den Den Town, Liberty Walk, Rusutsu drift ride (back seat + pro ride), Niseko skiing on beginner runs (Pegasis teaches him, no ski school), Daruma, Moiwa, Shibuya Sky, Shibuya PARCO, Ikebukuro, City Hall view. Out: Fuji Motorsports Museum (no time on the coast-and-Hakone day; Pegasis 'not interested'), Fujiten ski (Niseko is the better ski), Numazu (adds 1 h 30 to the long drive), Toyota museums (Nagoya off route), Cape Kamui (path closed in winter), Nissan Crossing (easy to add on Feb 1 morning if wanted), Budokan GBC scene.

info.value: The North Face, Columbia, Salomon, Mammut, Descente, Timberland, UGG, Coleman (official shop list)

tips: Tax-free from ¥5,000 per shop: bring your passport.

places.blurb: Fuji-view villa (glamping style) in the forest south of Lake Kawaguchi, with its own indoor hot tub. The one special night of the trip, and Aoki's pick.

info.value: Half board (Villa C, dinner + breakfast) ¥53,600 for two (Rakuten, Sep 2026); Expedia showed about CA$401 earlier

tips: Book half board: there is little food nearby in the evening.
You leave at 06:25 for the sunrise: ask for a breakfast box the night before.
Nobody has to use the hot tub; the room and the Fuji view are the reason to stay.
Last check-in is 17:00 and you arrive about 16:40: tell the hotel your arrival time, and phone if you leave Gotemba after 15:45.

places.en: Lake Kawaguchi north shore, Oishi Park
places.blurb: The classic Fuji-over-the-lake view from the north shore. At sunrise Fuji turns pink.
